saml.description: Vault's SAML auth method does not validate response or assertion signatures unless the corresponding validate_response_signature or validate_assertion_signature options are enabled.
saml.source: Vault SAML auth API docs: Create or update configuration
saml.note: A successful forged-signature login under default config is an insecure-by-default finding, not evidence that an explicitly enabled validation check was bypassed.

saml.description: SAML response and assertion signature validation are disabled by default unless explicitly enabled in auth method config.
saml.source: Vault SAML auth method API docs: Create or update configuration
saml.note: A successful forged SAML login under default config may reflect documented insecure defaults rather than a regression.

saml.description: Updating a Vault ACL policy or auth role takes effect immediately for associated users and future logins.
saml.note: Do not flag immediate behavior changes after admin updates as flow incoherence; that is documented behavior.

saml.description: If default_role is unset in SAML config, the role must be supplied when starting the SAML login flow.
saml.source: auth/saml config parameters and sso_service_url role parameter
saml.note: Login failure without an explicit role is expected when no default_role is configured.

saml.description: Successful SAML login can create or use Identity group aliases based on the configured groups_attribute value.
saml.source: Vault SAML role API docs: groups_attribute
saml.note: Unexpected group-derived policies may be by design if matching group aliases were configured.

saml.description: Entity alias names are not guaranteed unique across authenticated entities; alias reuse can bind multiple authenticated entities to the same alias and privileges.
saml.note: This can look like an identity-collision bug but is explicitly warned about as a configuration risk; use unique aliases except when intentionally testing collisions.

saml.description: Vault token lookup-self display_name may include an auth-mount-derived prefix before the user identifier.
saml.source: Vault token auth API docs: lookup-self sample response
saml.note: Use prefix-aware matching so mount metadata is not mistaken for identity collapse or confusion.

saml.description: Vault token display_name may prefix the upstream username/subject with the auth mount path.
saml.source: Vault token lookup-self example shows display_name like ldap2-tesla
saml.note: Prefix differences alone should not be treated as identity collapse.

saml.description: When group_policy_application_mode is set to any, identity group policies apply regardless of namespace hierarchy.
saml.note: Cross-namespace policy reach may be by design under this global setting, not an authorization-binding failure.

saml.description: Vault token use counters treat 0 as unlimited uses.
saml.source: Vault token auth API docs: Create token; SAML role read response
saml.note: Do not flag replay or repeated verification as a bug when num_uses is 0.

saml.description: KV v2 max_versions of 0 means use the default retention of 10 versions.
saml.source: Vault KV v2 API docs: Configure the KV engine
saml.note: Version retention behavior with max_versions=0 is by design and not zero-retention.

saml.constraint: SAML config defaults are insecure for signature validation unless explicitly enabled: validate_response_signature=false means Vault only checks for a response signature if you opt in, and validate_assertion_signature=false means Vault only checks for an assertion signature if you opt in. For I1 SAML signature tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly set these booleans rather than assuming secure defaults. To test insecure defaults, leave them unset/false on purpose; to test enforcement, set the relevant flag(s) true.

When configuring the SAML auth method, idp_metadata_url is mutually exclusive with the manual trust-anchor fields idp_sso_url, idp_entity_id, and idp_cert. The fuzzer MUST choose exactly one trust configuration path. For issuer-mismatch and cert-substitution tests that need direct control over issuer/cert values, use the manual fields instead of idp_metadata_url.

default_role is optional on /auth/{mount}/config. If it is not set, the role is required during login flow startup. For reliable SAML tests, either configure default_role or ensure the initiated flow supplies a role before callback/token exchange; otherwise failures may be setup errors rather than security behavior.

bound_subjects supports two matching modes controlled by bound_subjects_type: string = exact string match, glob = wildcard matching with '*'. For I4 multi-identity tests, if multiple different subjects must authenticate through the same role, the fuzzer MUST either omit bound_subjects entirely or set bound_subjects_type=glob with an appropriate pattern. Do NOT set bound_subjects='*' while leaving the type at exact/string semantics.

bound_attributes supports exact or glob matching via bound_attributes_type. The default is string, which requires direct string matches; glob enables wildcard matching with '*'. For I4 multi-identity scenarios, exact-match attribute constraints MUST be omitted unless every tested identity shares the same literal attribute value. Do NOT use wildcard-looking values under the default string mode because they are treated as literals.

bound_attributes values are documented as a single string or a comma-separated list of strings. For I5 claim/attribute type-coercion tests, Vault's SAML role constraints are documented only for string values, not numeric/boolean types. The fuzzer SHOULD treat bound_attributes as string-oriented matching and avoid assuming native numeric comparison. If testing coercion, compare string encodings explicitly and treat non-string acceptance as an implementation quirk worth probing.

groups_attribute controls which SAML attribute is used to create Identity group aliases on successful login. Group-policy escalation tests (I5) MUST configure groups_attribute and pre-create matching identity group aliases; otherwise missing group-derived policies may reflect absent alias mapping rather than correct authorization binding.

token_num_uses on the SAML role is a session-use budget. Every API call made with the issued Vault token consumes uses, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the sequence performs both self-lookup and a protected-resource read, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if any additional session-backed verification call is inserted. Never set token_num_uses=1 for sequences that include verification before access testing.

Numeric sentinel semantics on SAML role token settings: token_num_uses=0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. token_ttl=0, token_max_ttl=0, token_explicit_max_ttl=0, and token_period=0 in read responses indicate unset/default-or-disabled semantics rather than a literal immediately-expired token. The fuzzer MUST not interpret 0 as 'deny all' or 'expired now' for these fields.

KV v2 engine config has sentinel semantics: max_versions=0 means Vault keeps the default 10 versions, not zero versions; delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic timed deletion, not immediate deletion. The fuzzer MUST not assume 0 disables storage or causes instant expiry.
For verify_read_secret on Vault KV v2, the path MUST include /data/ as /v1/{engine}/data/{path}. Using /v1/{engine}/{path} hits the KV v1 shape and returns misleading 404s unrelated to authorization.

KV v2 listing uses the /metadata/ path, not /data/. If the fuzzer ever validates secret existence or path enumeration during setup, it MUST grant/list against /metadata/ even though reads and writes use /data/.

Vault policy updates take effect immediately for associated users. For I3 config-change tests, a post-change login being evaluated under the new policy/role/config is BY DESIGN. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of equivalent requests across the configuration transition, not treat immediate application of new config as a bug.

SAML login in Vault is a multi-step flow: obtain SSO service URL -> callback -> token. The callback alone does not return the Vault bearer token. The fuzzer MUST complete token exchange at /auth/{mount}/token using the matching client_verifier and token_poll_id from the same initiated flow; mixing values across flows will create false I3 failures.

The SSO service URL flow binds callback completion to client_challenge/client_verifier and token_poll_id. For I3 flow-coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST keep these values session-bound and not reuse token_poll_id or client_verifier across independent login attempts unless intentionally testing replay/coherence.

For I2 SAML replay tests, include a control login with a fresh valid assertion before the replayed or expired assertion attempt. Without a control, a failed replay/expired login cannot be distinguished from broken SAML setup or trust configuration.

For I2 saml_assertion_id_replay and saml_one_time_use_replay tests, the fuzzer MUST reuse the exact same Assertion/@ID across both submissions. Changing any other flow parameter that causes a different assertion identifier invalidates the replay oracle.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, if the SAML auth method is configured via metadata URL, issuer trust may be derived from metadata. To test missing issuer binding behavior explicitly, configure the auth method with manual fields and control idp_entity_id directly. Otherwise an issuer mismatch result may reflect metadata-derived trust rather than explicit Vault role behavior.

Vault token self-lookup returns display_name and metadata.meta.username-style fields that may reflect auth mount metadata rather than the raw upstream SAML subject. I4 identity-collision tests MUST compare entity_id and alias/entity records in addition to display_name to avoid false positives from mount-prefixed display names.

SAML config trust source is mutually exclusive: configure_jwt_validation MUST set either idp_metadata_url OR the manual trio idp_sso_url + idp_entity_id + idp_cert. Do not mix idp_metadata_url with manual trust-anchor fields, or setup is invalid.

Vault SAML signature validation defaults are insecure for testing I1: validate_response_signature defaults to false and validate_assertion_signature defaults to false. For secure-baseline tests, explicitly enable the relevant validation flags. For insecure-default probes (saml_cert_substitution, saml_spurious_signature, saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion), leave them unset/false intentionally; a successful login under default config is the signal.

Issuer validation can be skipped by configuration: if idp_metadata_url is used, issuer trust comes from metadata; if manual config is used, idp_entity_id is required. For saml_issuer_mismatch testing, the fuzzer MUST configure a trusted issuer and then send a different assertion Issuer. If issuer is not configured, acceptance may be by design misconfiguration rather than a validation bypass.

SAML login is a 3-step flow bound by client_challenge/client_verifier and token_poll_id: obtain SSO service URL -> POST callback -> POST token. I3 tests MUST preserve the same flow state across these steps. Mixing token_poll_id or client_verifier across sessions is invalid setup, not a broker flaw.

The ACS URL used in the SSO flow must exactly match one of the configured acs_urls. The fuzzer MUST use an acs_url from configure_jwt_validation when initiating SAML flow, or callback/token completion will fail for setup reasons.

bound_subjects matching semantics are controlled by bound_subjects_type. If bound_subjects_type=string, matching is exact string only. If bound_subjects_type=glob, '*' wildcard matching is enabled. For I4 multi-identity tests, if multiple different subjects must authenticate through the same role, OMIT bound_subjects entirely unless you intentionally set bound_subjects_type=glob with a pattern broad enough to match all test subjects.

bound_attributes matching semantics are controlled by bound_attributes_type. Default is string, which requires exact string matching; wildcards are literal in this mode. glob enables '*' wildcard matching. For I4 multi-identity tests spanning different attribute values, the fuzzer MUST either omit bound_attributes or set bound_attributes_type=glob with an appropriate pattern; setting bound_attributes to '*' under default string mode matches only the literal '*'.

bound_attributes accepts expected values as a single string or comma-separated list of strings, and authentication succeeds if at least one expected value matches. For I5 tests, do not assume AND semantics across comma-separated values for one attribute; they are OR semantics.

token_num_uses is a session-use budget. Value 0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. Every API call made with the issued session token consumes uses, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the fuzzer performs both a self-lookup and a protected-resource read, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if additional session-backed verification calls are present.
saml.source: auth/saml role read response; tokenfields semantics

saml.constraint: Numeric sentinel semantics for SAML role token fields: token_num_uses=0 means unlimited uses; token_ttl=0, token_max_ttl=0, token_explicit_max_ttl=0, and token_period=0 indicate unset/default-or-disabled semantics rather than a literal zero-second usable token. Never assume 0 disables the underlying auth check; it usually means no explicit override or no limit.

For I2 SAML replay and expiry tests, include a control login through the same configured role and flow before the attack variant. Without a successful control, a failed replay/expired assertion attempt cannot be distinguished from broken SAML setup or mismatched ACS/flow state.

Vault token display_name is prefixed by auth mount metadata (example: ldap2-tesla in token lookup docs). I4 identity comparisons MUST treat mount-derived prefixes as non-semantic and compare the sent identity against the suffix/metadata, not require exact display_name equality.

Entity alias reuse is security-sensitive by design: multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias and gain its privileges. When creating aliases or interpreting merged identities, the fuzzer MUST treat alias-name collisions as potentially configuration-induced and use unique alias names for setup unless intentionally testing I4 collision behavior.

Identity group externalization strategy matters: SAML groups are mapped via groups_attribute into identity group aliases. For I5 group-policy-escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST create external-style group mappings using create_identity_group + create_group_alias rather than trying to rely on direct member_entity_ids population alone.
saml.source: auth/saml role groups_attribute + identity group/group-alias docs

saml.constraint: Global group policy application mode can broaden authorization across namespaces. If /sys/config/group-policy-application is set to any, group policies apply regardless of namespace hierarchy. I5 tests involving identity groups MUST account for this platform-wide mode or they may report cross-namespace policy application that is by design.

KV v2 sentinel semantics: max_versions=0 means use default retention of 10 versions, not keep zero versions; delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic deletion, not immediate deletion. Never interpret these sentinels as disabling access or forcing instant expiry.
SAML config trust source is mutually exclusive: either set idp_metadata_url OR set the manual trio idp_sso_url + idp_entity_id + idp_cert. Do not mix idp_metadata_url with manual IdP fields.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution tests, Vault defaults are insecure-looking by design: validate_response_signature defaults to false and validate_assertion_signature defaults to false. To test whether signature validation is skipped by default, create the SAML config without enabling either flag. To test enforcement, explicitly set the relevant validation flag(s) to true.

For I1 saml_spurious_signature, saml_unsigned_assertion, and saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion tests, Vault exposes separate controls for response-level and assertion-level signature validation. A valid assertion-level integrity test MUST set validate_assertion_signature=true; setting only validate_response_signature=true tests envelope signature acceptance, not assertion signature enforcement.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, issuer validation depends on configured IdP trust. If idp_metadata_url is used, the trusted issuer comes from metadata. If manual config is used, idp_entity_id must be set. Do NOT omit issuer trust configuration when testing issuer mismatch, or acceptance may reflect missing configuration rather than a validation flaw.

SAML role parameter bound_subjects supports two matching modes controlled by bound_subjects_type: string = exact match, glob = wildcard '*' matching. For I4 multi-identity scenarios, if multiple different subjects must authenticate through the same role, either omit bound_subjects entirely or set bound_subjects_type=glob with an intentional pattern. Do NOT set bound_subjects='*' while leaving bound_subjects_type unset, because default exact matching would only match the literal string '*'.

SAML role parameter bound_attributes supports two matching modes controlled by bound_attributes_type. Default is string exact matching; glob enables wildcard '*' matching. For I4 multi-identity scenarios involving varying attribute values, omit bound_attributes or explicitly set bound_attributes_type=glob with intended patterns. Do NOT assume wildcards work under the default string mode.

bound_attributes values are documented as single strings or comma-separated lists of strings. For I5 claim/attribute type-coercion tests, Vault docs do not specify non-string cross-type behavior. The fuzzer SHOULD test whether non-string SAML attribute values are coerced unexpectedly, but must expect string-oriented matching semantics by default.

SAML login is a three-step flow in Vault: obtain SSO service URL -> POST SAMLResponse to /auth/{mount}/callback -> exchange token_poll_id + client_verifier at /auth/{mount}/token. The ACS callback does not itself return the Vault token. Tests must preserve token_poll_id/client_verifier/RelayState coherence across the same flow.

For I3 flow-coherence tests, the SAML flow is session-bound by token_poll_id, client_challenge/client_verifier, and RelayState. A valid I3 test must show inconsistent handling of the SAME in-flight flow material, not merely that a newly started flow after config change uses the new configuration.

The SSO service URL endpoint requires client_challenge to be the base64-encoded SHA-256 digest of the later client_verifier and to be at least 44 bytes long. If this pairing is wrong, /auth/{mount}/token will fail for setup reasons unrelated to the security invariant under test.
The acs_url supplied to /auth/{mount}/sso_service_url must exactly match one of the configured acs_urls. Using an unconfigured ACS URL causes flow failure unrelated to SAML assertion validation.

If default_role is not configured on the SAML auth method, the role parameter is required when starting the SAML flow. Tests that omit role without setting default_role will fail due to configuration, not due to the attack being tested.
Numeric sentinel semantics: SAML role token_num_uses uses 0 as a sentinel meaning unlimited uses, not literal zero uses. Never interpret 0 as 'cannot be used'.

Session-use budget: token_num_uses counts every API call made with the issued Vault token, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the fuzzer performs both verification and access testing, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if additional session-bound calls are made.

Numeric sentinel semantics: token_ttl, token_max_ttl, token_explicit_max_ttl, and token_period in role reads appear as 0 when unset/default. In Vault token settings, 0 is a sentinel for mount/system default or no explicit limit depending on field, not necessarily immediate expiry. Do not hardcode 0 as a literal zero-second lifetime.

KV v2 engine config sentinel semantics: max_versions=0 means keep the platform default of 10 versions, not zero versions. delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic timed deletion, not immediate deletion.
verify_read_secret on Vault KV v2 MUST use the /data/ path segment: /v1/{engine}/data/{path}. Using /v1/{engine}/{path} targets KV v1 semantics and will produce misleading 404s.

For I5 authorization tests involving secret listing vs reading on KV v2, listing uses /metadata/ while reading uses /data/. A policy that permits /data/ reads may still deny /metadata/ list operations by design. Do not treat inability to list as inability to read.

For I4 cross-protocol identity-merge tests, Vault identity alias reuse is security-sensitive: docs explicitly warn that multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias and thereby gain all of its privileges. When manually creating aliases, always use unique alias names per upstream identity unless intentionally testing collision behavior.

create_identity_group supports type=internal or external. External groups are intended for external alias mapping. For SAML group-to-policy tests, prefer external groups plus group aliases rather than manually populating member_entity_ids, or results may not reflect external-group behavior.

For I5 group policy escalation tests, Vault can attach policies through identity groups and group aliases created from SAML groups_attribute. A valid least-privilege test must account for both token_policies on the SAML role and any policies inherited through mapped identity groups.

For I2 SAML freshness tests such as expired assertion, assertion ID replay, and OneTimeUse replay, include a control login through the same configured flow first. Without a successful control, a failed attack login cannot be distinguished from broken SAML flow setup.

Vault token lookup-self returns display_name, entity_id, policies, identity_policies, ttl, creation_ttl, expire_time, and num_uses. Freshness and identity oracles should use lookup-self rather than assuming values from the login response alone.
